title: Goodbye, Eri
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Yuta Ito films his terminally ill mother at her request and is mocked when his movie ends with an exploding hospital. A classmate, Eri, who liked the film, persuades him to make another, and their semi-fictional documentary blurs memory, grief and storytelling, leaving what was real deliberately unclear.
life_message: Holds up art and memory as ways to honor the people we lose and to keep living after grief.

content.note: Cinematic explosions and implied family mistreatment; little graphic violence (to verify).
Terminal illness, deaths of family and grief throughout.
Some mockery and coarse speech among students (to verify).
Wikipedia describes two suicide attempts by Yuta, as a teen and an adult; AniList content signals flag suicide.
Bullying of Yuta by classmates; filmmaking as coping.

delivery.evidence: Wikipedia reception cites meta-cinema, self-reference and narrative trickery; what was real is left deliberately unclear.
delivery.note: Readers are left to infer what the film-within-the-story means about grief and memory.

winners_losers: Yuta survives by turning loss into film; the bullies and the abusive parent recede. Sympathy goes to the grieving artist and his friend.
